description: `plugin/governance/remediation-doctrine.md` `## First-Finding Triage` is the single source for the triage every remediation actor runs at the first non-trivial finding, before any fix. The source pin is the section heading. Seven further pins in the same file carry the load-bearing claims, each holding the key terms of a condition and its obligation. (1) The trigger and its obligation: at the first non-trivial finding, before any fix is planned or applied, answer four questions; moving the trigger after a fix or dropping the obligation turns the suite red. (2) The key: triage keys on the first finding, never on a finding count; re-keying it on a count turns the suite red. (3) Question 1's obligation: a found root cause is fixed at its source in the PR that found it, even outside the reviewed diff, and origin never licenses a deferral or a residual. (4) Question 2's obligation: the fix lands in the layer that owns the root class, not at the symptom. (5) Question 3's preference: removing or retiring the surface is preferred over hardening it. (6) Question 4's first condition and obligation: when a recorded threat model excludes the assumed attacker or failure, the finding is rejected at the source by citing the record and not hardened. (7) Question 4's second condition and obligation: when no threat model is recorded, recording one is a review call, asked or taken per `decision-autonomy.md` (Review Calls), when a reviewer raises it, and a call for the user otherwise. The consumers pin the POINTER only, never remedy prose, so honest rewording of the doctrine body does not break them: `plugin/agents/local-reviewer.md`, `plugin/agents/github-reviewer.md`, `plugin/agents/overlord.md` and `plugin/agents/cerebrate.md` must still cite the doctrine file with the section name `(First-Finding Triage)`. What this pin honestly guarantees is exactly that these word sequences exist in these five named files; it claims nothing about meaning. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) a meaning inversion that leaves the pinned bytes intact is invisible: surrounding prose that re-keys triage on a count, or that admits origin as a deferral ground elsewhere, stays green; (2) the bold question labels are unpinned, so renaming or deleting a label alone stays green; (3) a consumer can keep its pointer while moving the triage after its first fix, because the consumer pins carry the pointer and not the trigger wording around it; (4) the pin sees only the five files it names, and no fixture in this directory can detect a NEW remediation actor that never points at the section at all, which is an absence defect per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract.
